# BayesPrism deconvolution

BayesPrism is a standalone IOBRpy command. It is not part of the six-method TME bundle executed by `runall`.

## Inspect the command

```bash
iobrpy bayesprism --help
```

The input matrix must be genes by samples. Use the non-log matrix from STAR `runall`, not `03-tpm/tpm_matrix.csv`:

```bash
head results/gbm-demo/03-tpm/count2tpm.csv
```

## Run with the bundled reference

Choose the thread count after checking the host:

```bash
iobrpy bayesprism \
  --input results/gbm-demo/03-tpm/count2tpm.csv \
  --output results/gbm-demo/08-bayesprism \
  --threads 2
```

The output directory contains:

```text
08-bayesprism/
├── theta.csv
├── theta_cv.csv
└── Z_tumor.csv
```

- `theta.csv` contains the final cell-type fractions.
- `theta_cv.csv` contains posterior coefficient-of-variation values.
- `Z_tumor.csv` contains the inferred expression profile for the malignant-cell component.

The current implementation converts the input values to integers internally. The command above is a compact software tutorial using the non-log matrix produced by `runall`; it is not a validated reference-analysis design for this four-sample dataset.

## Use a custom single-cell reference

A custom reference requires a cell-by-gene count matrix, one cell-state label per cell, one cell-type label per cell, and a malignant cell-type key:

```bash
iobrpy bayesprism \
  --input bulk_expression.csv \
  --output bayesprism-custom \
  --threads 4 \
  --sc_dat single_cell_counts.csv \
  --cell_state_labels cell_state_labels.csv \
  --cell_type_labels cell_type_labels.csv \
  --key Malignant_cells
```

Reference genes, bulk genes, label order, and the tumor key must agree. Validate those inputs before interpreting the fractions.
